comments.content: Single-flight entry is not evicted on gate timeout, so late joiners share a doomed call and a hung judge leaks forever. `Promise.race([call.answers, timer.promise])` times out the waiter but `inFlight` still holds `call.answers` until the underlying judge settles. A new fire with the same `cacheKey` arriving after the timeout but before the judge settles gets `shared:true` and races the same stale promise. If the judge never settles, `judgeOnce`'s `then(delete,delete)` never runs and the entry leaks for process lifetime. Also `timer.promise` (a `withResolvers<never>`) stays pending on the success path — harmless but unnecessary. Fix: evict on timeout / settle the single-flight with timeout scope, e.g. wrap `judge.evaluate` itself in timeout before sharing, or `delete` + `clearTimeout` in the timeout branch.

Budget counts model calls, not fires, so D017 hard stop on number of fires is bypassable. The check sits after MPSE settlement and cache-hit early returns, and `budgetUsed` is only incremented for non-shared successful judgments (`if (!call.shared)` after the race). Cache hits, MPSE `IGNORE`, shared joins, and timeout/judge-error degradations (which throw/return before the increment) never consume budget. Retries or duplicates can thus process unbounded fires. Either rename/document `budgetFires` as an economic meter for model calls, or increment/check on every non-cached fire before judging.

Probability range is never validated — only finiteness is checked. `p<0` or `p>1` passes the guard, is banded (`p>1` always `act`, `p<0` always `ignore` regardless of fail polarity), cached via `cache.set`, and persisted to the ledger as if calibrated. This corrupts `calibration.ts` and lets a broken judge FIRE or DISMISS outside the contract. Treat out-of-range as `+bad-answer` (route by `failPolarity`), same as NaN/Infinity.

Degradation contract is fragile: substring matching + last-segment preservation. `includes('+no-answer')`/`includes('+fail-')` false-positives on legitimate policy names containing those substrings, collapses `+fail-open` vs `+fail-closed` to a single `JUDGE_UNAVAILABLE` (caller can no longer tell whether the degraded row FIRED or IGNORED), and `reroute` keeps only `match(/\+[^+]*$/)` so stacked degradations lose markers. Use exact suffix match (`endsWith`) or a structured field alongside `policyName`, and preserve the full `+...` chain on reroute.

Advisory fail-open conflates all throws into `verdict:pass, row:null`. Budget exhaustion (`GI_FIREGATE_BUDGET`), judge timeout, and judge errors all map to the same `GI_ADVISORY_OPEN` with no ledger row, so callers cannot distinguish 'judged safe' from 'never adjudicated' and calibration loses the attempt. Carry distinct `skipped.code` (e.g. `GI_ADVISORY_BUDGET` vs `GI_ADVISORY_OPEN:TIMEOUT`) and consider returning the degraded `row` when available instead of null.
Dead code: `all` is computed but never read. Remove it or use it for the mention scan.

### Top Issues

1. **Fire budget (D017) is bypassable — counts model calls, not fires** — `src/omp/fire-gate.ts`
   Check runs after MPSE settlement / cache-hit early returns, and `budgetUsed` only increments on non-shared successful judgments (`if (!call.shared)`). Cache hits, shared single-flight joiners, timeouts, and errors never consume budget, so an attacker / hot loop can fire unbounded without hitting the hard stop.

2. **Single-flight entry leaks on gate timeout** — `src/omp/fire-gate.ts`
   Waiters use `Promise.race([call.answers, timer.promise])` but `inFlight` still holds `call.answers` until the underlying judge settles. Late joiners attach to an already-timed-out call, and a hung judge pins the entry forever.

3. **Advisory fail-open erases failure reason** — `src/omp/fire-gate.ts`
   Budget exhaustion (`GI_FIREGATE_BUDGET`), judge timeout, and judge throws all collapse to `verdict:pass, row:null` / `GI_ADVISORY_OPEN` with no ledger row. Callers cannot distinguish `judged safe` from `never adjudicated`, and calibration silently degrades.

4. **Unvalidated probability range poisons cache + ledger** — `src/omp/fire-gate.ts`
   Only finiteness is checked; `p<0` / `p>1` passes, is banded (`p>1` always `act`, `p<0` always `ignore`), then `cache.set` + persisted as if calibrated. Corrupts `calibration` downstream.

5. **Fragile degradation contract via substring match** — `src/omp/fire-gate.ts`
   `includes('+no-answer')` / `includes('+fail-')` false-positives on legitimate policy names containing those substrings, and `+fail-open` vs `+fail-closed` collapses to a single `JUDGE_UNAVAILABLE`, losing caller-actionable polarity.

6. **Pre-act `theatrical` classification gap** — `src/omp/fire-gate.ts`
   `CLOSE_HINT.test(intent.tool)` tests tool name only, while `DESTRUCTIVE_HINT` tests `probe` (tool+target). `bash: 'ship it'` or `edit` on a close-like target never becomes `theatrical`. Also violates checklist ban on nested ternaries.

### Module Hotspots

- `src/omp/fire-gate.ts` — 7/7 comments in the scan. Sole hotspot; gate timeout / budget / fail-open / calibration logic all concentrated here and all safety-critical.
